text:
tess: quick check — I'm seeing weird truncation with streaming responses when a stop sequence appears right near max_tokens. stream closes and final token looks cut off.
max: can you paste the exact request you used? which endpoint and model?
tess: /v1/generate, streaming=true. params: max_tokens=64, stop=["\n\n"], temperature=0.7, top_p=0.9, logprobs=2. Example: short prompt that should stop on a blank line, but stream ends mid-word.
li: do you have the stream chunks? sometimes chunking + tokenizer boundaries cause partial bytes to be sent.
tess: i captured the stream. example chunks (simplified):
```
data: {"id":"r-1234","delta":"The quick brown fo"}
data: {"id":"r-1234","delta":"x jumps\n"}
data: [DONE]
```
so we get "fo" then next chunk finishes but then stream immediately [DONE] and we lose part of token in some runs.
sara: hmm. two possibilities: stop sequence matched and runtime closed before flushing final buffer, or max_tokens hit and we cut mid-token. which one looked more common?
tess: varied. sometimes stop triggered, sometimes max_tokens (if prompt was longer). unsure which rule took precedence.
oliver: @tess can you repro with max_tokens set way higher, see if stop alone still truncates? if yes it's likely stop vs stream flush.
tess: did that — with max_tokens=256 the stop still caused odd split occasionally.
max: note: we changed streaming flushing last month to emit partial chunks quickly for latency. that can expose tokenizer boundary races. server should wait for token boundary before emitting DONE, but maybe stop matching logic short-circuits.
li: quick workaround: set `return_full_text=true` (client-side merge) or don't rely on streaming for stop-sensitive short outputs.
sara: i'll create an eng-ml issue and flag as P1 if it's causing data loss for customers.
max: pls include request_id r-1234 + model name + canary/production flag. i'll check the runtime path where stop matcher calls `maybe_close_stream()`.
tess: thanks — adding reproducer and logs to the issue. also: one last question — does `logprobs` include partially emitted tokens if truncation happens?
max: logprobs are generated at token emission time. if the runtime truly truncates mid-token we'd drop that partial token and not include its logprob. but returning partial token is a bug. if you can reproduce with request_id i'll audit the emission pipeline.
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: canary deploy 2026-03-16T18:42 by infra-team applied to model `redwood-gpt-small` (tag: canary-2026-03-16)
li: FYI that deploy touched streaming buffer changes — might be correlated.
tess: noted. adding that canary tag to the bug report. thanks everyone :thumbsup: 
max: I'll take owner on the fix if logs confirm boundary race. will post updates in the issue and ping here when a patch lands.
sara: filed: ENGML-3421 — "streaming: stop sequence and max_tokens can cause mid-token truncation". assigned to max, priority P1. link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ENGML-3421
tess: awesome — closing loop here once fixed. appreciate the quick triage.
